Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators were found. Overall risk: **low** — however, the package appears to be a possible unofficial repackaging/variant of the official ultralytics package and should be verified.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

  • **low — possible official-package repackaging / brand-confusion risk**

- The package name is ultralytics-opencv-headless, but PKG-INFO points to the official ultralytics project in its description, authors, and project URLs.

- Name: ultralytics-opencv-headless

- Summary: Ultralytics YOLO ...

- Author-email: Glenn Jocher <glenn.jocher@ultralytics.com> ...

- Project-URL: Source, https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics

- The README/PKG-INFO installation instructions tell users to run pip install ultralytics, not this package name.

- This is not enough to conclude maliciousness, but it may represent a supply-chain confusion or repackaging pattern using a name similar to an official package. No malicious payload or theft behavior was confirmed from the provided input.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • The provided text corpus and pre-scan summary do not show evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, install-time setup.py/PEP 517 hooks, or interpreter-start automatic execution.
  • The README’s yolo CLI examples require explicit user execution and were treated as normal CLI behavior, not malicious automatic execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential theft:** No evidence of broad harvesting of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI/CD tokens, wallet files, or similar secrets was found.
  • **Staging/exfiltration:** No evidence of archive staging, temporary collection of harvested data, webhook upload, or attacker-controlled exfiltration endpoints was found.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of cron jobs, systemd units, launch agents, shell profile modification, or self-reinstall logic was found.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence involving Kubernetes service-account tokens, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, or GitHub Actions token abuse was found.
  • **Obfuscation/loaders:** The pre-scan reported eval/exec usage, but in the available context these appear related to model/framework configuration rather than an obfuscated loader, dropper, or staged remote payload.
  • Documentation links to raw.githubusercontent.com, GitHub release model files, and dataset URLs appear to be documentation/model/data download references and are not tied to credential theft or exfiltration.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • **Potential anomaly:** The package name is ultralytics-opencv-headless, while the metadata and documentation largely identify the official ultralytics package. This could be a legitimate variant, but the publisher’s authorization should be verified.
  • **Dependency change:** The use of opencv-python-headless>=4.6.0 appears consistent with the package name and was not judged malicious from the available evidence.
  • No direct evidence was provided for hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, or wheel/sdist behavior mismatch.

Additional Verification Needed

  • Only selected text from the 342 extracted files was provided. Static review of the actual pyproject.toml, setup.py, package __init__.py, entry point definitions, and any bundled binaries/large files is needed.
  • Verify whether the PyPI publisher is the official Ultralytics organization or an authorized maintainer.
  • Compare this sdist against the official ultralytics source for the same claimed version.
  • If a wheel exists, compare the wheel contents and behavior against the sdist.
